clue.text: Rocket's source of energy with ability to strafe the enemy

parts.note: a rocket is set off by fire, so its source is fire; Stephenson's Rocket locomotive also ran on a firebox
energy, in the physics sense, is also called power

explanation.surface: A clue about what drives a rocket and its capacity to strafe enemy positions.
explanation.definitionFit: Firepower is the destructive capacity of an armed force's weapons, the means of shooting at foes.

clue.text: Sweet nonsense

explanation.surface: Something sugary is just silly talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Fudge is a soft confection, and the exclamation fudge means rubbish or humbug.

clue.text: Fixed purpose to be always up' about sun-down

indicators.note: about places the reversed word around the sun's name
in a down clue, up means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: ever means always
Sol is the sun, here written downwards as normal in a down entry

explanation.surface: Determination to stay awake at all times around sunset.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolve is firm determination, a settled intent.

clue.text: An early death, that of H King's. medical advisers

definitions.text: An early death, that of H King's. medical advisers

parts.words: An early death, that of H King's. medical advisers
parts.note: in Belloc's cautionary tale, Henry King's physicians foretold that he would die young

explanation.surface: Recalling doctors who foresaw a young patient's demise.
explanation.walkthrough: Belloc's Henry King chewed string; the doctors said 'There is no cure for this disease. Henry will very soon be dead.'
explanation.definitionFit: A prognosis is a doctor's forecast of how an illness will turn out.

clue.text: On sea-trip we hear cham champagne's supply is inexhaustible

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece set on another sits above it

parts.note: the Widow is a nickname for Veuve Clicquot champagne

indicators.note: we hear says the voyage word is spoken, giving a similar-sounding word

parts.note: a cruise is a sea voyage

explanation.surface: Bubbly on a pleasure cruise apparently never runs out.
explanation.walkthrough: A cruse is an old word for a jar; in the Bible the widow of Zarephath's cruse of oil never emptied.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical widow's jar of oil never ran dry, so the phrase means a supply that never fails.

clue.text: This' race for survival needs speed out East

indicators.note: out says the compass letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: rate means speed

explanation.surface: The struggle to survive demands pace, except in the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a fill-in: the 'this' race for survival is the rat race, the competitive struggle of working life.
explanation.definitionFit: The rat race is the exhausting competitive scramble of modern working life.

clue.text: Picture border is to scale

explanation.surface: A framer's note on the edging round a painting being drawn in proportion.
explanation.definitionFit: A mount is the card surround framing a painting; to mount a hill is to climb or scale it.

clue.text: She of the frozen mitt caught by 'an impressionist

parts.note: Mimi is the heroine of La Bohème, to whom Rodolfo sings 'Che gelida manina', your tiny hand is frozen
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: An opera heroine with cold hands is captured by a painter like Monet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impressionist' suggests a painter, but here it is a performer who imitates voices.
explanation.definitionFit: An impressionist is an entertainer who imitates famous people, a copycat.

clue.text: Not knowing an end to peace in the French one

indicators.note: in places the article and the conflict inside the French word

parts.note: une is the French for one (feminine)
taken as written
war puts an end to peace

explanation.surface: Ignorant of a peace deal being concluded in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Unaware means ignorant or not conscious of something.

clue.text: Cheat with bridge winnings? Better to lose the stake

parts.note: in bridge, players win tricks

indicators.note: to lose says the wager is removed from the following word

parts.note: a bet is a stake

explanation.surface: Cardplayer asks whether to cheat with winnings, since betting means losing money.
explanation.definitionFit: A trickster is a swindler or deceiver.

clue.text: Canned music place has a way of making a horrid din

parts.note: a disco is a venue playing recorded, i.e. canned, music
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A complaint that a club playing recorded music makes an awful racket.
explanation.definitionFit: Discord is a harsh jarring mixture of sounds, a cacophony.

clue.text: Peter announces himself during half-time with drums

indicators.note: during says the self-introduction sits within the half of time
half of the hyphenated word time means its first two letters are kept

parts.note: Peter Pan introducing himself would say I'M PAN

explanation.surface: A boy named Peter introduces himself at the interval while drumming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'During' puts Peter Pan's self-introduction inside the first half of 'time'. 'Half-time' looks like a football interval, but it is half of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Timpani are kettledrums played in an orchestra.

clue.text: Some well-endowed lass for young Lochinvar

indicators.note: Some signals that only part of the following word's letters is taken

explanation.surface: A remark about a buxom girl being a match for a youthful hero.
explanation.walkthrough: In Scott's poem Marmion, young Lochinvar rides off with fair Ellen, his sweetheart.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellen is the girl that Lochinvar carries away from her wedding in Scott's ballad.

clue.text: Youth leader's pronounced expert with a witticism

indicators.note: pronounced says the letter name is to be said out loud, not written

parts.note: the leader of youth is its first letter Y, so 'Youth leader's' is Y's, said like a word meaning sagacious
crack, as an adjective, means expert or first-rate

explanation.surface: The head of a youth club, said to be very skilled, comes out with a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A wisecrack is a smart, flippant remark, a quip.

clue.text: Poet's 6 ac devours new poetry that's formalized

indicators.note: devours means the horse word swallows the rearranged letters

parts.note: 6 across is a mount; a poet's word for a horse or mount is steed

indicators.note: new signals the letters are made fresh in another order

explanation.surface: A poet's horse swallows fresh verse that is conventional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poet's 6 ac' means a poetic word for 6 across (MOUNT), which is STEED. 'New' is the anagram signal and 'devours' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Stereotyped means fixed in a conventional, unvarying form.

clue.text: "The fairest of her daughters. --"(, Milton)

parts.note: a gap to fill from Paradise Lost, where the first woman is called the fairest of her daughters

explanation.surface: A line of Milton quoted with its last word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Milton calls Adam 'the goodliest man of men since born his sons' and his wife 'the fairest of her daughters'.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton's line names the first woman as the loveliest of all her own female descendants.

clue.text: Unrehearsed beheading of next Manx emperor maybe

indicators.note: beheading removes the first letter of the following word
maybe suggests the remaining letters could be ordered differently
a Manx cat has no tail, so Manx means losing the last letter

explanation.surface: An Isle of Man ruler about to have his head cut off, without rehearsal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manx' cuts EMPEROR to EMPERO, which 'maybe' rearranges as EMPORE; 'beheading of' gives EXT.
explanation.definitionFit: Extempore means spoken or done on the spur of the moment, without preparation.

clue.text: Conrad's character appears mysteriously centre stage

indicators.note: mysteriously suggests the letters behave in an unexplained way and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A figure from a Conrad novel takes the spotlight in some puzzling way.
explanation.definitionFit: The Secret Agent is Joseph Conrad's 1907 novel, its title character the spy Verloc.

clue.text: Cynthia's excellent climbing, plant

parts.note: Cynthia is an epithet of Artemis, goddess of the moon

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the letters run upwards

parts.note: A1 means excellent, written here as AI

explanation.surface: A woman's excellent climbing plant.
explanation.walkthrough: Cynthia looks like a gardener's name, but it is Artemis, born on Mount Cynthus.
explanation.definitionFit: Artemisia is a genus of aromatic herbs including wormwood and mugwort.

clue.text: Answer — no end of pike in river that's like frosted glass

indicators.note: in places the answer and the fish inside the river's name

parts.note: the Trent is a major river of the English Midlands

indicators.note: no end of says the fish word loses its final letter

parts.note: a luce is a pike, especially a full-grown one

explanation.surface: A reply that a huge fish lives in a river with water clear as frosted glass.
explanation.walkthrough: The Trent is a major English river; luce is an old word for a pike. 'No end of' looks like the colloquial 'a great deal of', but here it cuts the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Translucent glass lets light through without being transparent, as frosted glass does.

clue.text: About to be put behind bars to this extent

indicators.note: About means the letters are turned around into a new order

parts.note: are is a form of the verb to be
to cage someone is to put them behind bars

explanation.surface: Someone is on the point of being jailed to such a degree.
explanation.definitionFit: Acreage is area measured in acres, the extent of a piece of land.

clue.text: Parade a vital necessity

explanation.surface: Showing off is something one cannot live without.
explanation.definitionFit: To air views is to parade them; oxygen-bearing atmosphere is something we cannot survive without.

clue.text: Contemptible fellow's subscribed to article in Belgium

indicators.note: subscribed means written underneath, so in a down entry this piece comes below

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
a twerp is a silly, contemptible person

explanation.surface: A despicable man has signed up to a newspaper piece in Brussels.
explanation.definitionFit: Antwerp is a major port city of Flanders.

clue.text: Mikado's prisoners providing such fun?

parts.note: in Gilbert and Sullivan's Mikado, each prisoner pent is made to represent a source of innocent fun

explanation.surface: Wondering whether the convicts in a comic opera are entertaining.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mikado's song 'A more humane Mikado' says each prisoner pent will 'unwillingly represent a source of innocent merriment'.
explanation.definitionFit: Merriment means fun and jollity, the very word from the Mikado's song.

clue.text: Wall-climber with gold hidden in this tower?

indicators.note: hidden says the metal is concealed within the climbing plant

parts.note: ivy is a plant that climbs walls
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A creeper with treasure concealed in a tower.
explanation.walkthrough: An ivory tower is a retreat from practical life.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase ivory tower describes an unworldly, sheltered academic existence.

clue.text: Skill Demosthenes acquired in place of prayer

explanation.surface: The Greek statesman learned an art in a chapel.
explanation.definitionFit: Demosthenes famously trained himself in public speaking; a small chapel for private worship has the same name.

clue.text: Letter sent up by this beast

indicators.note: in a down clue, sent up means written from bottom to top

parts.note: kay is the spelt-out name of the letter K

explanation.surface: A message dispatched by an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A yak is a long-haired Tibetan ox.

clue.text: Johnson's horse's knee in his ignorance

definitions.text: Johnson's horse's knee in his ignorance

parts.words: Johnson's horse's knee in his ignorance
parts.note: Dr Johnson's Dictionary wrongly defined a part of a horse's leg as its knee, which he put down to pure ignorance

explanation.surface: Remembering a famous lexicographer's blunder about equine anatomy.
explanation.walkthrough: Asked why he had defined this as a horse's knee, Samuel Johnson replied, 'Ignorance, madam, pure ignorance.'
explanation.definitionFit: The pastern is actually the part of a horse's foot between fetlock and hoof, not the knee.

clue.text: See about, for instance, a poem

indicators.note: about says the bishopric's name goes round the abbreviation for instance

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city, a bishop's see
EG is the abbreviation of exempli gratia, for instance

explanation.surface: An instruction to look around, with a poem offered as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: An elegy is a mournful poem, typically a lament for the dead.

clue.text: One involved in ransom demand and conversely in fish

indicators.note: in places the turned-round word inside the fish

parts.note: a kipper is a smoked herring

indicators.note: conversely means the word and is turned the other way round

explanation.surface: Someone mixed up in an extortion plot, and the other way about, in a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ransom demand' tempts you to look for a fish hidden inside it, but it is part of the definition; 'conversely' reverses the little word 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who abducts a person typically demands money for their return.
